[@pijanowski2011] with the first description of the 3 main types of sounds in the soundscape: The ‘soundscape’ includes all sounds emanating from any given habitat, which can be classified with respect to their source: geophony (climate and geography), biophony (all wildlife), and anthrophony (human activities), to be added technophony [@fuller2015] linked to the uses of machine from car to industrials

Acoustic signals within the soundscape include sounds from living organisms (biophony), natural sounds from physical processes (geophony), and sounds caused by human activities (anthrophony) (Pijanowski et al., 2011).

 Acoustic indices are a type of quantitative soundscape analyses used to rapidly assess ecosystem condition by deriving a numeric summary of the soundscape.
Ecological meaning is inferred by relating acoustic indices to the diversity of vocalizing taxa via species richness or other diversity metrics (Gasc et al., 2013;Eldridge et al., 2018;Dröge et al., 2021) or to habitat quality via landscape or vegetation characteristics (Fuller et al., 2015;Sánchez-Giraldo et al., 2021;Sangermano, 2022).
